$comment: The resource trees a distributable package must carry. Single source: scripts/release_assembly.py derives VIDEO_RUNTIME_RESOURCES from the video entries, frontend/scripts/audit-production-package.mjs derives its required-resource assertion from all of them, and scripts/check_release_package_wiring.py derives the release wiring gate from the same file. Adding a sixth resource here is what makes every one of those gates start demanding it.

resources.name: embedded-browser
resources.$comment: macOS: the bundler follows symlinks and destroys the Chrome for Testing framework, so this tree is installed after the bundle is built by release_assembly.install_and_seal. Windows has no symlinks and an NSIS installer cannot be reopened, so it is declared and copied by the bundler instead. Per-file integrity is proven against the EB-05 manifest by release_assembly.require_packaged_browser and scripts/check_embedded_browser_package.py; this contract only fixes where it must land.

resources.name: local-executor
resources.$comment: The only resource the macOS bundler ships, and the reason an empty bundle.resources must never pass. Its inner inventory and manifest signature are proven by frontend/scripts/audit-release-bundle.mjs and the executor package manifest schema.
